solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Equipment, on rupture trapping acceleration line, forces jumper closer to drop (13)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, X on Y puts X after Y
indicatorNotes.trapping: the rupture holds the next letters inside it
indicatorNotes.closer: the closer of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: a para is a paratrooper, the forces' jumper

annotation.surface: A skydiving kit list: the gear, the risk of injury and the moment the jumper leaves the plane.
annotation.walkthrough: The skydiving picture makes 'forces jumper' read as a description of someone at the plane door, when it is the source of letters. A para is a paratrooper, so a forces jumper.
annotation.definitionFit: Paraphernalia is the equipment or gear needed for an activity.

entries.clue: It’s assumed posties rip up redirected letters regularly in town (14)

annotation.definitionNote: a clause standing for the noun: a presupposition is something that is assumed

indicatorNotes.redirected: the letters are sent off in a new order
indicatorNotes.regularly: something done regularly happens at even intervals, so the letters are taken at even steps through the word

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters of tOwN

annotation.surface: Townsfolk take for granted that postmen tear up and misroute their mail.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rip up' looks like the anagram indicator, but it is fodder; 'redirected' does the mixing, fitting the postal picture. A posty is a British colloquial word for a postman.
annotation.definitionFit: A presupposition is a thing tacitly assumed beforehand.

entries.clue: Quick wry jape — bit odd, they’re all naked! (5)

indicatorNotes.they’re all naked: each word is stripped of its outer letters, like clothes

annotation.surface: A cheeky joke that ends with everyone undressed.
annotation.walkthrough: Four words each lose their first and last letter; the exclamation in the surface is the instruction, since naked words have lost their covering.
annotation.definitionFit: Rapid and quick both mean fast.

entries.clue: Divisive work boosted city revolt (10)

indicatorNotes.boosted: in a down clue, pushed up means read from bottom to top

annotation.surface: A contentious piece of art that has stirred a city to rebellion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boosted' reads as praise for the work, but in a down entry it lifts OP to PO.
annotation.definitionFit: Something polarising splits opinion into opposed camps, so it is divisive.

entries.clue: Timber, length truncated and vein across width (7)

indicatorNotes.truncated: cut short: the last letter goes
indicatorNotes.across: the vein lies across the W, taking it inside

blocks.note: ELL, an old measure of length, minus its last letter
vein = mood, as in 'in a playful vein'

annotation.surface: A carpenter noting a plank cut short, with a streak running across its grain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vein' looks like a streak in the wood, which suits the timber surface, but it means a mood or tone.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: elm is one of many trees whose wood is sold as timber.

entries.clue: Regularly unwound with bonus puzzle (7)

indicatorNotes.Regularly: something done regularly happens at even intervals, so the letters are taken at even steps through the word

blocks.note: second, fourth and sixth letters of uNwOuNd
a plus is a bonus, an extra advantage

annotation.surface: Someone relaxing with a prize crossword.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Puzzle' reads as a noun in the relaxation picture, but the definition is the verb: to nonplus is to baffle.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: both mean to leave someone baffled and unsure what to say.

entries.clue: Abandoned amphibian down from loch (4)

indicatorNotes.down from: in a down entry, the amphibian sits below the loch letter

annotation.surface: A newt deserted and washed downstream from a Scottish lake.
annotation.walkthrough: EFT, an old word for a newt, is a crossword regular worth knowing.
annotation.definitionFit: Abandoned and left both mean deserted.

entries.clue: Claim key and lock up; no one coming round (9)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, the lock is read from bottom to top
indicatorNotes.coming round: the letters turn back on themselves

blocks.note: a lock of hair is a tress

annotation.surface: Securing a building with a key when no one is expected to visit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Key and lock' are a pair in the surface, but 'lock' is hair, not a door fitting.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain noun synonym: both are statements put forward as true.

entries.clue: Top business accommodating guests? (7,7)

blocks.note: a parent firm that owns the shares of the companies below it

annotation.surface: A leading hotel firm.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second reading: split the phrase into its two words and it describes a host with a house full of company.
annotation.definitionFit: A holding company is the parent firm at the top of a group of companies.

entries.clue: Throw out old regressive record, Lulu’s first (5)

indicatorNotes.regressive: regressing is going backwards, so the record's letters are read in reverse
indicatorNotes.first: Lulu's first is the first thing in her name, its opening letter

annotation.surface: Binning an old-fashioned record by the singer Lulu, her debut.
annotation.walkthrough: Lulu is a Scottish pop singer, so 'old regressive record' reads as a dated song rather than three pieces of wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym, as when a school or party removes a member.

entries.clue: One fellow is in France, plugging country cycling policies (9)

annotation.definitionNote: plural for singular: a manifesto is a published set of policies

indicatorNotes.plugging: the first pieces fill a gap in the country
indicatorNotes.cycling: the first letter moves round to the end

annotation.surface: A man in France plugging a nation's green transport plans.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cycling policies' pretends to be about bikes; 'cycling' belongs to the country, moving its first letter to the back. The inserted pieces go in before the final letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose collective sense: an election manifesto is the document in which a party lists its policies.

entries.clue: Lured down, confused, crossing River Styx here? (10)

indicatorNotes.confused: a confused mind has things in the wrong order, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.crossing: the jumble reaches across the river letter, holding it

annotation.surface: A soul tricked into descending and ferried bewildered over the Styx.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the journey of the dead, so the wordplay and the scene are the same thing; 'here?' points at the place the Styx flows.
annotation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Styx is a river of the underworld, the realm of the dead.

entries.clue: Raised money on podcast (4)

indicatorNotes.on podcast: a podcast is heard, not read

annotation.surface: Fundraising done through a podcast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Raised money' looks like one phrase about fundraising; split it, and 'Raised' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Bred means raised, as children or livestock are.

entries.clue: S&M pictures perhaps in flyer (4,6)

blocks.note: the ampersand spelt out: S AND M
pictures are one kind of art

annotation.surface: Racy images printed in a leaflet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' plays on a handbill, which fits the racy surface; it is the bird. Read '&' as the word AND.
annotation.definitionFit: A sand martin is a small burrow-nesting swallow, a bird and so a flyer.

entries.clue: Did squeeze bishop’s backside beneath robes, without introduction (7)

indicatorNotes.backside: the back end of the word, its last letter

blocks.note: beneath robes = DRESSED, minus its first letter

annotation.surface: A scandalous pinch of a bishop's bottom under his vestments.
annotation.walkthrough: Anyone beneath robes is dressed; dropping its D leaves RESSED after the P.
annotation.definitionFit: Pressed is the past tense of press, to squeeze.

entries.clue: Parts of blowers, hammers and anvils etc? (9)

blocks.note: blower is British slang for a telephone
the hammer and anvil are tiny bones of the ear

annotation.surface: An inventory from a blacksmith's forge: bellows, hammers and anvils.
annotation.walkthrough: The forge picture hides both senses: a blower is British slang for a phone, and the hammer, anvil and stirrup are the bones of the middle ear.
annotation.definitionFit: Earpieces are parts of phones held to the ear, and the ear's bones are, loosely, its pieces.

entries.clue: Street apartment evacuated on gathering lead from information channel (7)

annotation.type: charade + outer letters + container + first letter

indicatorNotes.evacuated: emptied, leaving only the outer letters
indicatorNotes.gathering: the pieces take the next letter inside them
indicatorNotes.lead from: the lead is what goes in front, so the opening letter of information

annotation.surface: Residents cleared from a flat, gathered round for news from a broadcaster.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On' is not a link here: it is the letters themselves, and it joins the emptied apartment before the pair gathers the lead letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A broadcasting sense: a radio or TV station is the channel you tune to.

entries.clue: Phone in say, about plant (7)

indicatorNotes.in: a thing put in something ends up inside it, so the phone letters sit within the other word
indicatorNotes.about: the letters are turned about into a new order

annotation.surface: A radio phone-in segment discussing a garden plant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Phone in' looks like a radio show, but the two words do separate jobs; 'say' is not 'for example' here but the letters themselves.
annotation.definitionFit: Syringa is the lilac, a flowering shrub.

entries.clue: Workers’ digs? (7)

blocks.note: the surface wants human labourers; the setter means worker ants
digs is British slang for rented lodgings, and also what ants do to make a nest

annotation.surface: Lodgings for labourers.
annotation.walkthrough: Workers are worker ants, and digs, British slang for lodgings, also fits a home that ants dig out.
annotation.definitionFit: An anthill is the mound home of a colony of ants.

entries.clue: Pleasure-seeking romantic in ode, hurt somewhat on the rebound (7)

indicatorNotes.somewhat: only some of the words' letters are used
indicatorNotes.on the rebound: the letters come back the other way

annotation.surface: A lover pouring hurt into a poem after a breakup.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On the rebound' fits the jilted lover and is the reversal instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A formal adjective from the same Greek root as hedonist, a person who lives for enjoyment.

entries.clue: You saw some four or more roe deer or moose? (7)

annotation.definition: You saw some four or more roe deer or moose?

blocks.clueFragment: You saw some four or more
blocks.note: the surface wants a count of animals; each word also sounds like another word: ewe, sore, sum, for, oar, moor
roe, deer and moose sound like row, dear and mousse; the question mark flags the examples

annotation.surface: A wildlife spotter asking whether you saw several roe deer or a moose.
annotation.walkthrough: There are no letters to build: the clue is a string of examples, every word of it paired with a different word of the same sound.
annotation.definitionFit: Homonyms are words that sound or are spelt like other words with different meanings.

entries.clue: Fool facing Chaser in game, more than one losing round (4)

indicatorNotes.facing: two things facing each other stand side by side, so the pieces are placed next to one another
indicatorNotes.losing: what a word loses is taken away from it, so the round letter comes out

blocks.note: TWO, more than one, minus O, a round letter
in the game of tag, whoever chases is 'it'

annotation.surface: A quiz contestant up against the Chaser, hopelessly outnumbered.
annotation.walkthrough: The Chase is a British TV quiz whose resident experts are Chasers, but here the chaser is 'it' in playground tag.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain noun synonym, twit being a mild British insult for a silly person.

entries.clue: Location of collection — small pound outside US city university centre of mathematics (5,5)

indicatorNotes.outside: the first pieces go round the city
indicatorNotes.centre of: the centre of a word is the letter at its exact middle

blocks.note: sixth, middle letter of the eleven in mathematics

annotation.surface: Where an American city's university keeps a small pound and a maths centre.
annotation.walkthrough: S and LB wrap round TAMPA; 'pound' looks like a verb or money but is the weight abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a philatelist's stamps are mounted in the book, so it is where the collection lives.

entries.clue: British hooligan scratching walls in African thatched hut (5)

indicatorNotes.scratching walls: the hooligan's outer letters are scratched off

blocks.note: VANDAL minus its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A lout defacing the walls of a hut on an African trip.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scratching walls' is exactly what a vandal does, which is why it hides the instruction to remove VANDAL's outer letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A banda is a thatched hut found in parts of Africa.

entries.clue: Swallow filling when somersaulting (4)

indicatorNotes.somersaulting: turning head over heels, so the letters go the other way

blocks.note: a plug is a filling for a hole

annotation.surface: Having trouble swallowing a pie filling while tumbling.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' could be the bird doing aerial tumbles, but it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym, gulping being hasty, noisy swallowing.

entries.clue: US colonic shifted blockage of passage (9)

annotation.surface: An American colon cleanse that cleared an intestinal blockage.
annotation.walkthrough: The medical surface is so literal it barely disguises the definition; the trick is noticing that 'US colonic' has the same nine letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A medical term: doctors speak of the occlusion of an artery or airway when it is closed off.

entries.clue: As far as tips of northern Greenland’s Arctic island group (5)

indicatorNotes.tips of: the tip of each word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letters of northern, Greenland's, Arctic

annotation.surface: An Arctic island group at the far northern tip of Greenland.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all polar, but the answer is in the South Pacific.
annotation.definitionFit: Tonga is a Polynesian kingdom made up of a group of islands.

entries.clue: Extra flexible workforce attempt to secure area (13)

indicatorNotes.to secure: the attempt holds the area letter inside it

annotation.surface: Hiring a flexible extra workforce to lock down a site.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flexible workforce' reads as one labour-market phrase, and even 'Extra' could be casual staff, but the two words give separate pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain adjective synonym, as in a supplementary charge on a bill.
